figures.item: The UK tax year the figures below belong to. It runs 6 April to 5 April, not the calendar year. Corporation tax uses a financial year from 1 April instead.
figures.quote: The current tax year is from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027.

figures.item: Standard Personal Allowance: income each individual may have before income tax. England, Wales and Northern Ireland; the allowance is the same in Scotland, only the rates and bands differ. Per person, not per couple. Frozen at this amount to the end of 2027 to 2028.
figures.quote: The standard Personal Allowance is £12,570, which is the amount of income you do not have to pay tax on.

figures.item: Adjusted net income at which the Personal Allowance starts to be withdrawn. Not a cliff: the allowance tapers away above this figure.
figures.quote: Your personal allowance goes down by £1 for every £2 that your adjusted net income is above £100,000.

figures.item: The taper rate for the Personal Allowance above the income limit, as gov.uk prints it. It is a ratio, not a percentage: the allowance falls by GBP 1 for each GBP 2 of adjusted net income over the limit.
figures.quote: Your personal allowance goes down by £1 for every £2 that your adjusted net income is above

figures.item: Adjusted net income at or above which the Personal Allowance is nil. Same number as the additional rate threshold, but this is the allowance rule, not the rate band.
figures.quote: This means your allowance is zero if your income is £125,140 or above.

figures.item: Basic rate of income tax on non-savings non-dividend income, England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Scotland has six bands and different rates.
Width of the basic rate band, that is taxable income after the Personal Allowance has been deducted. Not the income figure: the income figure is GBP 50,270.
figures.quote: Basic rate 20% Up to £37,700 Up to £37,700

figures.item: Total income at which the basic rate band ends for someone with the standard Personal Allowance. Also the Class 1 upper earnings limit and the Class 4 upper profits limit.
Higher rate of income tax on non-savings non-dividend income, England, Wales and Northern Ireland.
figures.quote: Higher rate £50,271 to £125,140 40%

figures.item: Additional rate of income tax on non-savings non-dividend income, England, Wales and Northern Ireland.
figures.quote: Additional rate over £125,140 45%

figures.item: Total income above which the additional rate applies. The HMRC rates publication prints the same band as 'Over £125,141'; the taxpayer page prints 'over £125,140'.
figures.quote: Additional rate over £125,140 45%

figures.item: Dividend allowance: dividend income taxed at 0% before the dividend rates bite. It is an allowance inside the bands, not an extra band, and it uses up part of whichever band it falls in.
figures.quote: You also get a dividend allowance of £500 each year.

figures.item: Dividend ordinary rate, on dividends above the dividend allowance that fall in the basic rate band. RAISED from 8.75% for 2026 to 2027 by Budget 2025; applies to distributions made on or after 6 April 2026, UK-wide including Scotland.
figures.quote: Tax band Tax rate on dividends over the allowance Basic rate 10.75%

figures.item: Dividend upper rate, on dividends in the higher rate band. RAISED from 33.75% for 2026 to 2027; applies to distributions made on or after 6 April 2026, UK-wide.
figures.quote: Basic rate 10.75% Higher rate 35.75%

figures.item: Dividend additional rate, on dividends in the additional rate band. UNCHANGED at this rate for 2026 to 2027.
figures.quote: Higher rate 35.75% Additional rate 39.35%

figures.item: Starting rate band for savings interest, taxed at 0%. Available only while other taxable income (excluding savings interest and dividends) is below GBP 17,570, and reduced GBP 1 for GBP 1 by other income above the Personal Allowance.
figures.quote: This means you can earn up to £5,000 of interest and not have to pay tax on it.

figures.item: Other taxable income below which any starting rate for savings is available at all.
figures.quote: If your other taxable income (not including savings interest or dividends) is less than £17,570, you can get the starter rate for savings.

figures.item: Personal Savings Allowance for a basic rate taxpayer: interest taxed at 0%. Separate from, and on top of, the starting rate band.
figures.quote: Income Tax band Personal Savings Allowance Basic rate £1,000 Higher rate £500

figures.item: Personal Savings Allowance for a higher rate taxpayer.
figures.quote: Basic rate £1,000 Higher rate £500 Additional rate £0

figures.item: Personal Savings Allowance for an additional rate taxpayer: there is none.
figures.quote: Basic rate £1,000 Higher rate £500 Additional rate £0

figures.item: Savings income is taxed at the ordinary basic, higher and additional rates for 2026 to 2027. The separate savings rates of 22%, 42% and 47% start only from 6 April 2027, so do NOT use them for tax year 2026.
figures.quote: Since April 2017 the rates have been 20% for basic rate taxpayers, 40% for higher rate taxpayers, and 45% for additional rate taxpayers.

figures.item: Savings basic, higher and additional rates, FUTURE. They apply from 6 April 2027 for the 2027 to 2028 tax year, UK-wide. Do NOT use them for tax year 2026, when savings income is still taxed at 20%, 40% and 45%.
figures.quote: The rates for the 2027 to 2028 tax year will be: the savings basic rate at 22% the savings higher rate at 42% the savings additional rate at 47%

figures.item: Property income basic, higher and additional rates, FUTURE. Separate rates for letting income start 6 April 2027 in England, Wales and Northern Ireland. For tax year 2026 property income is taxed at the ordinary 20%, 40% and 45%.
figures.quote: The rates for the 2027 to 2028 tax year will be the property basic rate at 22% the property higher rate at 42% the property additional rate at 47%

figures.item: Trading allowance: gross self-employment or casual income that can be received tax free. Full relief below it (no tax return needed for that income alone); above it the allowance may be deducted INSTEAD of actual expenses, never as well.
figures.quote: You can get up to £1,000 each tax year in tax-free allowances for property or trading income from 6 April 2017.

figures.item: Property allowance: gross property income that can be received tax free. A separate GBP 1,000 from the trading allowance; someone with both types of income gets both. Cannot be used with the Rent a Room Scheme on the same income.
figures.quote: If you have both types of income, you’ll get a £1,000 allowance for each.

figures.item: Gross sole trader income above which a Self Assessment return is required. Same number as the trading allowance, but this is the filing trigger, not the deduction.
figures.quote: you were self-employed as a ‘sole trader’ and earned more than £1,000

figures.item: Marriage Allowance: the fixed slice of Personal Allowance a lower earner may transfer to a spouse or civil partner. All or nothing, not a chosen amount.
figures.quote: Marriage Allowance lets you transfer £1,260 of your Personal Allowance to your husband, wife or civil partner.

figures.item: The most Marriage Allowance can reduce the receiving partner's tax by in a tax year.
figures.quote: This reduces their tax by up to £252 in the tax year

figures.item: High Income Child Benefit Charge: the adjusted net income of the higher-earning partner at which the charge starts. Per individual, never household income added together.
figures.quote: If you or your partner earn more than £60,000 a year, you’ll have to pay some of your Child Benefit back.

figures.item: High Income Child Benefit Charge: adjusted net income at which the whole of the Child Benefit is clawed back.
figures.quote: If you or your partner earn £80,000 or more, you’ll have to pay all of it back.

figures.item: High Income Child Benefit Charge: the clawback step. 1% of the Child Benefit for each GBP 200 of income over the threshold. For years up to 2023 to 2024 it was 1% per GBP 100 over GBP 50,000.
figures.quote: You’ll pay back 1% of your Child Benefit for every £200 you earn over the threshold.

figures.item: Payments on account are not required if last year's Self Assessment tax bill was below this amount. A cliff: at or above it, both instalments are due.
figures.quote: the amount of tax you owed last year was less than £1,000

figures.item: Payments on account are also not required if more than this share of last year's tax was collected outside Self Assessment, for example through a tax code.
figures.quote: last year you paid more than 80% of the tax you owed outside of Self Assessment

figures.item: Each payment on account is half of the previous year's Self Assessment bill, due 31 January and 31 July. Class 4 National Insurance is included; Class 2 and capital gains tax are not.
figures.value: half of the previous year's tax
figures.quote: Each payment is half of the tax you owed last year.

figures.item: Self Assessment late filing penalty, charged the day after the filing deadline even if no tax is owed.
figures.quote: an initial £100 penalty

figures.item: Self Assessment late filing: daily penalty once the return is 3 months late.
figures.quote: after 3 months, additional daily penalties of £10 per day, up to a maximum of £900

figures.item: Cap on the GBP 10 daily late filing penalties (90 days).
figures.quote: additional daily penalties of £10 per day, up to a maximum of £900

figures.item: Self Assessment late filing: penalty at 6 months late, the GREATER of 5% of the tax due or GBP 300.
figures.value: 5% of the tax due or GBP 300, whichever is greater
figures.quote: after 6 months, a further penalty of 5% of the tax due or £300, whichever is greater

figures.item: Self Assessment late filing: a second penalty at 12 months late, again the greater of 5% or GBP 300. It is on top of the 6-month penalty, not instead of it.
figures.value: 5% of the tax due or GBP 300, whichever is greater
figures.quote: after 12 months, another 5% or £300 charge, whichever is greater

figures.item: Self Assessment late payment penalties: 5% of the tax still unpaid at each of 30 days, 6 months and 12 months. Three separate 5% charges, and interest runs as well.
figures.quote: You’ll get penalties of 5% of the tax unpaid at: 30 days 6 months 12 months

figures.item: How HMRC sets late payment interest on income tax, National Insurance, capital gains tax, corporation tax self assessment and VAT: Bank of England base rate plus a fixed margin. The margin was 2.5% on or before 5 April 2025.
figures.quote: late payment interest set at base rate plus 4% from 6 April 2025

figures.item: The late payment interest rate HMRC prints as current. Read the page before quoting it: it moves with the Bank of England base rate and this is the rate shown on 19 September 2026.
figures.quote: late payment interest rate — 7.75% from 9 January 2026

figures.item: How HMRC sets repayment interest on tax it holds and must give back.
figures.quote: repayment interest, set at base rate minus 1%, with a lower limit of 0.5%

figures.item: The repayment interest rate HMRC prints as current on 19 September 2026.
figures.quote: repayment interest rate — 2.75% from 9 January 2026

figures.item: Minimum repayment interest rate, the 'minimum floor', whatever the base rate does.
figures.quote: with a lower limit of 0.5% (known as the ‘minimum floor’)

figures.item: Class 1 primary threshold, yearly. Same number as the Personal Allowance, but it is a National Insurance threshold, not an allowance.
figures.quote: Primary threshold £242 per week £1,048 per month £12,570 per year

figures.item: Class 1 secondary threshold, yearly. Far below the employee threshold: an employer pays from GBP 5,000 while the employee pays from GBP 12,570.
figures.quote: Secondary threshold £96 per week £417 per month £5,000 per year

figures.item: Class 1 upper earnings limit, yearly.
figures.quote: Upper earnings limit £967 per week £4,189 per month £50,270 per year

figures.quote: Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit A 0% 8% 2%

figures.item: Employee Class 1 rate on earnings above the upper earnings limit, category letter A.
Employer (secondary) Class 1 rate, category letter A, on all earnings above the secondary threshold. There is no upper limit for the employer.
figures.quote: Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit, upper secondary thresholds for under 21s, apprentices and veterans A 15% 15% 15% 15% B 15% 15% 15% 15%

figures.item: Class 1A rate the employer pays on taxable benefits in kind reported on form P11D, and on termination awards above GBP 30,000.
figures.quote: Class 1A rate on expenses and benefits for 2026 to 2027 is 15%.

figures.item: Employment Allowance: the most an eligible employer can knock off its employer Class 1 National Insurance bill in the year. It is a reduction of liability, not a cash payment, and a one-director company with no other employee cannot claim it.
figures.quote: Employment Allowance for 2026 to 2027 is £10,500.

figures.item: Class 2 small profits threshold. At or above it Class 2 contributions are TREATED AS PAID, so the year counts for the State Pension and nothing is payable.
figures.quote: If your profits are £7,105 or more a year Class 2 contributions are treated as having been paid

figures.item: Class 2 weekly rate. For 2026 to 2027 it is only payable VOLUNTARILY, by someone with profits below the small profits threshold who wants the year to count.
figures.quote: The Class 2 rate for tax year 2026 to 2027 is £3.65 a week.

figures.item: Class 3 voluntary weekly rate, used to fill a gap in the National Insurance record where Class 2 is not available.
figures.quote: £3.65 a week for Class 2 £18.40 a week for Class 3

figures.item: Class 4 lower profits limit: self-employed profits above this pay Class 4.
figures.quote: If your profits are more than £12,570 a year, you must pay Class 4 contributions.

figures.item: Class 4 main rate on self-employed profits between the lower and upper profits limits.
figures.quote: For tax year 2026 to 2027 you’ll pay: 6% on profits over £12,570 up to £50,270

figures.item: Class 4 upper profits limit: above it the rate drops to 2%.
figures.quote: 6% on profits over £12,570 up to £50,270 2% on profits over £50,270

figures.item: Class 4 rate on profits above the upper profits limit.
figures.quote: 6% on profits over £12,570 up to £50,270 2% on profits over £50,270

figures.item: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, first wave. Qualifying income (GROSS self-employment and property income, before expenses) over this figure in the 2024 to 2025 tax year means quarterly updates from 6 April 2026.
figures.tax_year: tested on 2024 to 2025 income; start 6 April 2026
figures.quote: £50,000 for the 2024 to 2025 tax year, you should’ve started using Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2026

figures.item: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, second wave: qualifying income over this figure in 2025 to 2026 means joining from 6 April 2027.
figures.tax_year: tested on 2025 to 2026 income; start 6 April 2027
figures.quote: £30,000 for the 2025 to 2026 tax year, you will need to use it from 6 April 2027

figures.item: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, third wave: qualifying income over this figure in 2026 to 2027, the current tax year, means joining from 6 April 2028. This is the test a 2026 return will be measured against.
figures.tax_year: tested on 2026 to 2027 income; start 6 April 2028
figures.quote: £20,000 for the 2026 to 2027 tax year, you will need to use it from 6 April 2028

figures.item: Flat Rate Scheme: reduction of the sector rate during the first year of VAT registration.

figures.quote: When you reach the threshold, you’ll receive a £200 penalty.

figures.item: First late payment penalty for VAT: nothing up to day 15; 3% of what is outstanding at day 15 if paid between day 16 and day 30; and if still unpaid at day 31, a further 3% of what was outstanding at day 30 on top.
figures.tax_year: VAT periods starting on or after 1 January 2023

figures.item: Partial exemption de minimis, first limb: exempt input tax no more than this on average each month (GBP 7,500 a year). BOTH limbs must be met.
figures.quote: You can be treated as fully taxable in any tax period or longer period (section 12) if the total value of your exempt input tax is not more than: £625 per month on average

figures.item: Partial exemption de minimis, second limb: exempt input tax no more than half of total input tax in the period.

figures.quote: The CGS applies to capital expenditure on land and buildings with a value of £600,000 or more (exclusive of VAT )

figures.quote: The CGS also applies to capital expenditure on aircraft, ships, boats and other vessels with a VAT exclusive value of £50,000 or more

figures.item: A simplified VAT invoice may be issued where the value of the supply is at or below this amount and the customer agrees.

figures.item: Annual investment allowance: 100% deduction for qualifying plant and machinery in the year of purchase. Available to sole traders, partnerships and companies. NOT available on cars, on items owned before the business used them, or on gifts. Pro-rated for a period that is not 12 months.
figures.quote: The AIA amount is £1 million.

figures.item: Full expensing: 100% first-year deduction on new and unused main-rate plant and machinery. COMPANIES ONLY, and never on cars. A sole trader uses the annual investment allowance instead.
figures.quote: Full expensing lets you deduct 100% of the cost of qualifying plant and machinery from your profits before tax in the year it was bought.

figures.item: 50% first-year allowance on new and unused SPECIAL RATE plant and machinery, for example integral features. Companies only; the remaining 50% goes into the special rate pool.
figures.quote: The 50% first-year allowance lets you deduct 50% of the cost from your profits before tax in the year it was bought.

figures.item: NEW 40% first-year allowance on main-rate plant and machinery bought on or after 1 January 2026. It must be new and unused and not a car; the remaining 60% is written down in later periods. Unlike full expensing this is open to unincorporated businesses as well.
figures.quote: If you buy plant or machinery that qualifies for 40% first-year allowance, you can deduct 40% of the cost from your profits before tax.

figures.item: Main pool writing down allowance. CUT from 18%: the new rate applies from 1 April 2026 for corporation tax and 6 April 2026 for income tax, and a period straddling that date needs a hybrid rate.

figures.quote: special rate pool with a rate of 6%
